This can be a time-consuming process, but it's crucial to separate what's worth keeping from what's not. Here are some tips to help you get started: ### **The One-Year Rule** Consider the one-year rule when deciding what to keep. If you haven't used an item in the past year, it's likely safe to get rid of it. Ask yourself: - When was the last time I used this item? - Do I still have a purpose for it? - Can I replace it if needed? If the answer is no, it's probably safe to throw it away. Here are some items that are worth keeping: - Family heirlooms and sentimental items - Items with sentimental value - Items that are still in good condition and useful - Items that bring joy or serve a purpose ### **Preserving Memories** When it comes to sentimental items, it's essential to preserve memories rather than cluttering your space. Consider the following: - Keep a limited number of sentimental items that hold significant value - Take photos of items you want to remember but don't have space for - Donate or store items that are still in good condition but no longer needed ### **Useful Items** Keep items that are still in good condition and serve a purpose. This might include: - Kitchen gadgets - Tools - Furniture - Books Consider repurposing items to give them a new life. For example, turning old pallets into a coffee table or upcycling old jars for storage. **What to Throw Away** Not everything deserves to be kept. Here are some items that are safe to throw away: - Broken or damaged items - Expired or unused items - Duplicate items - Items that no longer serve a purpose ### **Getting Rid of Hazardous Materials** When decluttering, it's essential to dispose of hazardous materials safely.
